guitar.notes: Hugh Cornwell is known for playing Fender Telecasters with The Stranglers.

tone.target: jangly clean edge-of-breakup with arpeggiated delay
tone.profile: jangly clean edge-of-breakup with arpeggiated delay
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain utilizing light compression, a Chorus effect for width, and an AC30-style amp paired with a 2x12 cabinet to achieve the required chime and clarity, topped off with Digital Delay for the arpeggiated feel.

rig.name: The Stranglers - Golden Brown - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain clarity for arpeggios.
Provide light compression to smooth dynamics and enhance the 'polished' sound.
Add width and vintage shimmer to the clean arpeggios.
Keep the tone clean and avoid any mid-gain crunch or heavy distortion.
Emulate the bright, chimey sound of a Vox AC30, crucial for the 'bright chime' requirement.
Provide a bright and articulate sound suitable for clean arpeggios.
Slightly boost the high end and cut unnecessary low-end rumble to emphasize chime.
Create the 'arpeggiated delay' feel and add rhythmic depth without sounding muddy.
Add a subtle, polished ambience without losing the dry, bright character.

improvements.summary: Upgrade cabinet IR to better capture the vintage chime and brightness of a Vox AC30.

proposals.reason: The US 2x12 is too generic; a Vox-specific IR will enhance the required chime and vintage character.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and authentic AC30 sparkle.
